- Keyboard: with a key-press effect on, the keyboard's window grew as tall as the screen while typing, so the app above was pushed up by all of it and an empty strip showed between the page and the keys. The effect is drawn only inside the keyboard now, so the page keeps the room above the keys and the text you type stays in view.
- Downloads, Series: every season shows a picture of its own without any key: the still of its first episode, cut upright and sharp (before, every season showed the same series poster until a TMDB key was given). With a TMDB key in the Download manager settings the season's own poster is shown as before.
- Downloads, Series and movies: the results of the name search come by themselves as the name is typed (a moment after the last letter); the Find button is gone.
- Keyboard: it remembers numbers you type again and again (a phone number, an ID number) and offers them from the first two digits, on the bar, also in number fields; a tap writes the rest. A number of 7 to 19 digits counts when it is finished (Enter, space, or the field is left); it is offered from the second time. They are kept on the phone only (never backed up), never from password fields or a PIN box, never in private typing, and a card number (it passes the card check) is never kept. Settings > Keyboard > Numbers I type often shows them, one can be added or removed, "Forget all" clears them, and the switch turns it off.
- Password vault: Pulse is an autofill service again (Android 8 and newer; Passwords and autofill > pick Pulse, or the new "Use Pulse for autofill" button in the vault): the logins of the vault are offered in other apps and in browsers, and a login typed in a form is offered to the vault. Only one autofill service can be on at a time, so it stays off until you pick it. A login in a vault that is behind the screen lock shows its password only after the phone's lock (fingerprint, face or PIN) is answered.
- Password vault: cards. A saved card is offered in a payment form (number, expiry, security code, holder), always after the phone's lock is answered. "Offer to save card numbers" in the vault (off at first) lets a card typed in a payment form be saved into the vault when you say so: only a number that passes the card check, never twice.
- Everything in the vault is sealed with the key of this phone (AES-GCM, a file private to Pulse, left out of every backup). The numbers the keyboard remembers (the setting above) are sealed the same way now instead of kept as plain preferences; the ones an earlier build kept are moved into the sealed file.
